context:
Goal: No record tells a session to mint a credential the app ignores, and you can still recover the ledger from a backup.
Problem (rule): About fifteen records and CLAUDE.md still tell a reader to put a GitHub token on each device. The app no longer writes to GitHub and no device holds a token. Retiring them needs a ruling on one form: a dated Retired line, or none.
Based on (read): mailaudit docs/decisions/live-verification.md:13 says no device holds a token; src/entry.jsx has no token screen, though it still sends a stored token on GitHub calls when one exists (entry.jsx:354-366) (main cd3e12f).
Based on (notes): Not run live; unmeasured at runtime. Worker snapshots protect recovery; web History still reads GitHub.
Departs from: These records say a token goes on every device and the app has none — each is marked retired and its first sentence rewritten, with one dated Retired line allowed.

options.gain: No session mints a token; one clear retirement form.
options.how: Mark each retired in docs/records.md, rewrite its first sentence, keep older-versions-come-off-branch live, allow one dated Retired line and reword CLAUDE.md:167.
options.label: Retire, dated line allowed
options.lose: A dated line stays in retired records, which a stricter rule would delete.

options.gain: Retired records carry no history text.
options.how: Same retirement, and delete any Retired line.
options.label: Retire, no Retired line
options.lose: The reader loses the date; more edits to the records.

ref: deep audit 1102, mailaudit homes; coordinator handoff/audit-child-questions 9d97c9b, github-era-records-retire
title: mailaudit: Retire the GitHub-token records, one dated line?
why: Recommended in the audit report: retire, one dated line allowed.
